name: assignment 7/help.c
summary: Find the smallest even and odd values in four inputs. The source uses nested decisions. The brief incorrectly calls zero neither odd nor even; mathematically zero is even, while this exercise explicitly excludes it. New validation follows the brief’s two-even/two-odd, nonzero input assumptions.

name: assignment 10/helper.c

name: assignment 11/assign11.c

name: assignment 12/assign12.c

name: assignment 13/assign_13.c

name: assignment 16/assign16.c

The new tokenizer is a bounded explanation and does not certify the original three methods as equivalent.

name: assignment 17/assign17.c
summary: Connect nested records to dynamically allocated character storage. assign17.c allocates only one byte for a school name and scans an unbounded string. The related heap exercise shows a pointer table and cleanup but needs input/buffer checks. The model uses fictional student labels, never real identity numbers.

name: assignment 17/heap.cpp
summary: C++ max-heap exercise. The insertion loop reads eight elements from a seven-element array; compilation alone misses this out-of-bounds access.

name: final assignment/fassign.c
summary: Follow pthread_create, fork, exec, wait and join in the submitted program. The original joins t1 before creating t2. The submitted university screenshot shows the combined name, a ps listing and child status 0. A controlled local retest returned ps status 1. execlp lacks a proper argv[0], waitpid receives NULL instead of integer 0, and error/status checks are incomplete. The visual trace distinguishes intended success from this observed nonzero result.
